title: One core concurrency law: open a thread whenever work can run at once; lanes first-class
action: USER DIRECTIVE 2026-07-28, verbatim intent: parallel is already the headline rule for cells, but LANES stay hidden — promote them to the same level, add a real planning check for what can run concurrently, and collapse everything into ONE core rule: if several pieces of work can run at the same time, open the threads and run them; run serially only when forced. Ship fast. IMPLEMENT: (1) AGENTS.md '## Communication' section stays untouched; add a SHORT rule to the critical-rules list (or extend the existing parallel rule if one is there) stating the core law in one sentence plus its three tiers — gather work fans out to I/O workers, cells of a slice fan out to a wave, and independent FEATURES fan out to lanes (bee state start-feature --as-lane --paths ...) or worktrees. AGENTS.md budget: root is ~15.4KB against 18KB warn / 20KB hard — keep the addition under ~700 bytes and edit the TEMPLATE plus the rendered root (see scripts/tests/test_agents_budget.mjs for both paths, they must stay byte-identical). (2) skills/bee-hive/references/routing-and-contracts.md: rewrite the parallel doctrine section into the full protocol under this one law: (a) THE LAW and its three tiers; (b) MANDATORY CONCURRENCY PLAN — before dispatching anything, the orchestrator states in one line what runs concurrently and what is forced serial and why; the plan is computed, not guessed: cells from `bee cells schedule` (declared file overlap), features from declared --paths (the lane guard refuses a real overlap, which is the machine proving the answer); (c) THE ONLY LEGAL REASONS FOR SERIAL, exhaustive: declared file-set overlap (including shared generated artifacts not deferred by a wave barrier), a true data dependency (deps), a single scarce external resource, or an explicit human instruction — anything else is not a reason and the work fans out; (d) LANES, first-class: when new feature work is ready while another feature is live and their paths are disjoint, the paved road is a lane, NOT a queue — `bee state start-feature --feature <f> --mode <m> --as-lane --paths <declared>`; lane-scoped mutations take --lane; a lane refusal names the holder and is itself the concurrency plan's evidence; worktrees remain the answer when the work needs its own checkout; (e) TICK: the concurrency plan emits its own progress line per the Progress ticks catalog. Fold any existing 'serial stays the default' or lane-as-exception wording into this — one law, no second list. (3) skills/bee-hive/SKILL.md: the triage/routing text must route new-feature-while-busy to a lane instead of waiting, in <=2 lines, pointing at the reference section. Body budget 8180 recorded, ceiling 8192 — net-zero-or-negative, trim to pay. NOTE: this cell deliberately does NOT touch packages/bee (a sibling feature holds it) — code affordances land in a follow-up cell. R82: run NO test suites; cap --feature-verify-pending; MAIN verifies at close.
